answer: DeepWalk tends to do better on the word analogy task because it learns embeddings from random walks that capture higher-order, multi-step co-occurrence patterns in the graph, which are more similar to the kind of relational regularities needed for analogies. LINE(2nd), by contrast, is designed mainly to preserve second-order proximity, i.e., local neighborhood similarity, and it does not model the same broader context structure as effectively. On Wikipedia, where the graph is large and sparse, DeepWalk’s skip-gram-on-walks objective can exploit longer-range structural information and produce embeddings that are more transferable to analogy relations than LINE(2nd)’s more local objective.
